bbc.description: Forty people have drowned in heatwave-related deaths in France since last Thursday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says.

bbc.description: Traffic in the waterway has risen since the US and Iran signed a deal aimed at ending the war, including 42 ships on Saturday alone.

bbc.description: It is suing the US defence department after it was added to a list of firms with ties to the Chinese military.

bbc.description: Edgar Lungu's family and the Zambian government remained in dispute 12 months after he died.

bbc.title: Spider which uses spring trap to capture prey discovered in Australia
bbc.description: Researchers say their hunting method - which allows them to prey on dangerous ants - is unprecedented.

bbc.description: The former Louisiana inmate argued his Rastafarian faith was violated after prison officials focibly shaved off his hair.

bbc.description: The money will come from the last allocation from the Irish government's Shared Island Fund.

bbc.title: Trump anticipates better relationship with Colombia under new leader
bbc.description: Abelardo de la Espriella, who preliminary results suggest is Colombia's next president, had Trump's endorsement.

bbc.title: Montreal shooting leaves officer, civilian and suspect dead
bbc.description: It was the first time in 24 years that a Montreal police officer was  killed in the line of duty, the city's police chief said.

bbc.title: Ransom note claims Nancy Guthrie died after abduction
bbc.description: On Tuesday, Today show presenter Savannah Guthrie begged anyone with information to come forward, saying, "We are in agony."

bbc.title: Iran says no new commitments on nuclear sites after Vance says inspectors to be invited back
bbc.description: Iran's foreign ministry says it made "no new commitments" on nuclear inspections after talks in Switzerland.

bbc.title: Dettol apologises after ad to clean up 'toxic men' backfires in China
bbc.description: The ad sparked accusations of sexism in China, after featuring a man looking for a partner who is "not tainted by other men".

bbc.title: Inquiry ordered after building fire kills 15 in north India city
bbc.description: Witnesses described people jumping from windows to escape, while rescue teams broke through a wall to save lives.

rfi.title: France scrambles to respond, as June heatwave grips Europe
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is to hold a crisis meeting on Tuesday, after Météo France reported that the country's average temperature had broken a June record. Elsewhere in Europe, several countries are also struggling with the heatwave, which has led to a number of deaths and disruption to public services.

rfi.title: EU gambles on Taliban talks to fast-track Afghan deportations
rfi.description: A Taliban delegation is due to fly into Brussels on Tuesday, having been granted a one-day visa to hold talks with the EU on returning failed asylum seekers to Afghanistan. However, human rights groups have warned that the scheme runs counter to the bloc's values.

rfi.title: Blood minerals and memory: the Great Lakes in focus
rfi.description: This week, Spotlight on Africa turns to the Great Lakes region. First, a new Global Witness report reveals how coltan is being smuggled out of the Democratic Republic of Congo, amid the ongoing conflict in the east, through Rwanda and on to companies worldwide. Then, artist Grada Kilomba discusses her journey to create a unique monument for Paris commemorating the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: 'Export trade has increased since exiting the EU, it's been a win'
rfi.description: Ten years after the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, Brexit remains one of the most contested political decisions in recent British history. Its legacy is increasingly shaped by diverging interpretations of sovereignty and the UK's place in the world. RFI spoke to Brexit supporter Robert Oulds, director of British think tank the Bruges Group, about what has changed.

rfi.title: Brexit at 10: the promises, the costs and the search for accountability
rfi.description: Ten years on, the UK's decision to leave the European Union is increasingly seen as more than a single referendum result. Critics argue it reflected a wider crisis of political imagination, with Brexit supporters misreading both Britain and the world, while the promised future never arrived.

rfi.title: Resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch enters Paris's Pantheon
rfi.description: French resistance fighter and historian Marc Bloch will be inducted into the Pantheon in Paris on Tuesday, giving President Emmanuel Macron another chance to shape France’s national memory through one of the Republic’s most symbolic ceremonies.

rfi.title: Mbappé's double on 100th appearance fires France into World Cup knockout stages
rfi.description: Kylian Mbappé marked his 100th cap for France on Monday night with two goals in their 3-0 win over Iraq in a game that took more than four hours to complete due to thunder storms over Philadelphia.

rfi.title: Messi notches up World Cup goals record to take Argentina into knockout stages
rfi.description: Argentina skipper Lionel Messi added another accolade to his otherworldly list of achievements on Monday when he became the record goalscorer at World Cups since the inception of the tournament in 1930

rfi.title: Haaland scores twice as Norway outwit Senegal to reach last 32 at World Cup
rfi.description: Erling Haaland scored twice on Monday night as Norway advanced to the knockout stages at the World Cup following a pulsating 3-2 victory over Senegal in New Jersey.

rfi.title: Repeated errors in handling of rape case linked to French girl's death: report
rfi.description: An administrative investigation ordered after the death of 11 year-old Lyhanna in southern France has revealed serious failings in how a previous rape complaint against the main suspect was handled. The case has brought the French judicial and police system under stark scrutiny, especially regarding cases of child abuse.

rfi.title: 'Poison in your coffee' report sounds alarm over widespread pesticide use
rfi.description: Coffee production around the world depends heavily on pesticides, leaving millions of farm workers exposed to harmful chemicals while pesticide residues are also found in exported coffee beans, a report published on Monday warned.

rfi.title: Paris court rejects bid to reopen probe into Caribbean chlordecone contamination
rfi.description: The Paris appeals court has upheld a decision not to reopen a criminal investigation into the use of chlordecone, a toxic pesticide that has been linked to cancer and other health problems in around 90 percent of the adult population in Guadeloupe and Martinique.

rfi.title: UN warns of an 'imminent risk of mass atrocities' in Sudan's Kordofan
rfi.description: In Sudan, NGOs and the UN have warned of an "imminent risk of mass atrocities" in El-Obeid, a major city in North Kordofan. This comes as the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) step up their campaign against the regular army in the region.

rfi.title: France, Germany reach deal on arms maker KNDS, opening door to stock market
rfi.description: France and Germany announced Monday a deal for the joint governance of Amsterdam-headquartered arms maker KNDS, paving the way for a blockbuster share offering as they seek to boost faltering European defence cooperation.

rfi.title: France's scorching weekend heat leads to elderly deaths and spate of drownings
rfi.description: The deaths of three elderly people in southwestern France have been linked to the heatwave hitting the country, while authorities have reported an increase in drownings, as people seek relief from the heat in rivers and lakes.

rfi.title: UK's Starmer resigns as prime minister
rfi.description: UK leader Keir Starmer announced his resignation on Monday following months of pressure, kickstarting a process that will see Britain get its seventh prime minister in a decade.

rfi.title: DRC announces free healthcare for all illnesses in Ituri as Ebola gains ground
rfi.description: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has announced the introduction of free healthcare for all diseases in Ituri – a pilot project that authorities hope to extend nationwide. This comes as the country struggles to contain an Ebola outbreak, with confirmed cases now at over 1,000.

rfi.title: Ethiopia’s ruling party wins another large majority in parliament
rfi.description: Ethiopia's ruling party has won over 90 percent of seats in parliament, according to official results announced three weeks after the election.

euronews.title: Airbus under fresh scrutiny as EASA orders A380 inspections over wing cracks
euronews.description: The aviation giant is already battling supply chain problems and growing costs across its operations.

euronews.title: Cristiano Ronaldo scores at his sixth World Cup
euronews.description: Cristiano Ronaldo scored as Portugal beat Uzbekistan in their World Cup group match in Houston, becoming the first footballer to score at six World Cup tournaments.

euronews.title: Giant Messi statue honors Argentina's World Cup hero
euronews.description: A giant mural near Buenos Aires and a towering statue in Patagonia highlight Lionel Messi's enduring status as a symbol of unity and pride for Argentines during the World Cup.

euronews.title: Belgian royals roll out red carpet for Japan's emperor
euronews.description: Japanese Emperor Naruhito and Empress Masako received a ceremonial welcome at the Royal Palace of Brussels as they began a state visit to Belgium.

euronews.title: UNAIDS warns Trump's HIV funding cuts to South Africa could cost lives
euronews.description: The Trump administration says the phased withdrawal is linked to policy disputes with Pretoria, which rejects the allegations and says it is pursuing greater self-reliance.

euronews.title: Nicotine pouch sales surge among young people, watchdog warns
euronews.description: Flavoured, promoted on social media, discreet and unregulated: sales of addictive nicotine pouches are booming among youth. A global tobacco industry watchdog, STOP, warns that this could lead to a new wave of nicotine addiction.

euronews.title: Iceland kills first whales since 2023, resuming whaling
euronews.description: Iceland's Marine and Freshwater Research Institute has recommended that no more than 150 fin whales are caught in the 2026 season.

euronews.title: Japan's emperor and empress arrive in Belgium for state visit
euronews.description: The arrival of Japan's emperor and empress in Belgium marks a symbolic moment for two countries whose partnership stretches back more than a century and a half.

euronews.title: Von der Leyen to visit Pashinyan in Yerevan to build on Armenia’s pro-EU vote
euronews.description: As the EU rolls out a support package for Armenia, European Commission President von der Leyen is set to meet re-elected Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan after he secured a decisive pro-West mandate from the Armenian people, sources confirmed to Euronews.

euronews.title: UN launches Hormuz evacuation for 11,000 stranded seafarers
euronews.description: The operation follows a peace agreement between the United States and Iran that ended months of conflict and allowed commercial shipping to resume through one of the world's most important maritime routes.

euronews.title: Latest news bulletin | June 23rd, 2026 – Evening
euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this June 23rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: EU officials discreetly meet Taliban in Brussels to speed up Afghan deportations
euronews.description: EU officials and Taliban representatives held a technical meeting in Brussels to discuss the return of Afghan nationals in a fresh attempt to ramp up repatriations of migrants without the right to stay in Europe.

euronews.title: From Bolsonaro and Bukele to Fujimori and De la Espriella: Trump and Latin America's rightward turn
euronews.description: Soon after the US president first moved into the White House, his policies and outspoken backing for certain candidates inspired a new wave of Latin American leaders now shaping the continent’s future.

euronews.title: LEGO's Julia Goldin named first-ever European CMO of the Year at Cannes Lions
euronews.description: Chosen by more than 800 marketing leaders from across Europe, Julia Goldin was recognised for helping transform LEGO into a global cultural brand through partnerships spanning entertainment, gaming and sport.

euronews.title: Armenia and Azerbaijan agree landmark internet deal as peace process continues
euronews.description: Armenia and Azerbaijan’s leading telecom companies agreed to a joint internet transit project as both countries move forward together after decades of war, boosting regional connectivity.

euronews.title: Versailles unveils gallery for 250th anniversary of US independence
euronews.description: Opening on Saturday 4 July, this gallery brings together paintings, sculptures and portraits from the château’s collections to spotlight the political, diplomatic and military figures of independence.

euronews.title: How Israel became a test case for the EU's institutional battle over foreign policy
euronews.description: Diverging views on the EU's relations with Israel are exposing a growing rivalry between the European Commission and top diplomat Kaja Kallas over who sets the bloc's foreign policy, undermining its overall coherence.

euronews.title: Spain toughens rules for e-scooters: new requirements
euronews.description: The government has approved a reform to the General Traffic Regulations making helmets compulsory for e-scooter users nationwide and setting a minimum age of 15. The measure forms part of a road safety package.

lemonde.title: Vincent Jeanbrun, ministre du logement : « Le défi est de mieux accompagner l’adaptation des logements aux pics de chaleur »
lemonde.description: Dans un entretien au « Monde », le ministre expose les points-clés de son projet de loi destiné à augmenter l’offre d’habitations et présenté, mercredi, en conseil des ministres. Il esquisse également des pistes pour faire face aux canicules.

lemonde.title: Marc Bloch au Panthéon : revivez la cérémonie d’hommage à l’historien et résistant
lemonde.description: Quatre-vingt-deux ans après son exécution par la Gestapo, le 16 juin 1944, Marc Bloch est entré mardi 23 juin au Panthéon. Emmanuel Macron a honoré ses « enseignements qui nous obligent », contre « l’esprit de défaite ».

lemonde.title: Autonomie de la Corse : le principe a été approuvé par l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: C’est Gérald Darmanin, alors ministre de l’intérieur, qui avait été chargé par Emmanuel Macron de mettre sur pied le projet de loi, pour mettre un terme aux violences provoquées par la mort en prison du militant indépendantiste Yvan Colonna.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : la « loi intégrale » inscrite à l’agenda de l’Assemblée nationale, une victoire pour les féministes et les enfantistes
lemonde.description: Le texte, qui doit permettre de mieux lutter contre les violences sexistes et sexuelles, sera examiné à l’automne, a annoncé le premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, après un changement de pied. Un examen du Conseil d’Etat devrait cependant amener à changer les contours du projet de loi.

lemonde.title: Le Congrès américain ordonne à Donald Trump de retirer les troupes américaines impliquées dans le conflit avec l’Iran
lemonde.description: Le Sénat a adopté, mardi, une résolution déjà approuvée par la Chambre des représentants. Quatre élus républicains se sont joints aux voix démocrates. Même si le texte est symbolique, il s’agit d’un camouflet pour le président américain.

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : Icône fragilisée, Cristiano Ronaldo amorce timidement son retour en grâce
lemonde.description: Vivement critiqué après son premier match, le capitaine portugais a inscrit un doublé, mardi 23 juin, et contribué à la large victoire (5-0) de sa sélection face à l’Ouzbékistan. Il est le premier joueur à avoir marqué lors de six Coupes du monde.

lemonde.title: En Allemagne, le trafic ferroviaire reprend après une panne qui a immobilisé les trains dans tout le pays
lemonde.description: « Nos ⁠experts en informatique ont travaillé sans relâche pour résoudre ⁠ce ‌problème et ils y sont ​parvenus », a annoncé un porte-parole de la Deutsche Bahn, l’opérateur national des chemins de fer, précisant que le trafic ⁠reprenait ‌graduellement.

lemonde.title: Au Soudan, la crainte d’un assaut des paramilitaires sur El-Obeid
lemonde.description: Huit mois après la prise sanglante d’El-Fasher, la capitale du Kordofan du Nord pourrait à son tour tomber aux mains des Forces de soutien rapide. Depuis début juin, les paramilitaires mènent une intense campagne de bombardements aériens sur la ville.

lemonde.title: En Hongrie, Péter Magyar lance l’« opération purgatoire » pour tourner la page de Viktor Orban
lemonde.description: Un mois et demi après l’investiture du nouveau premier ministre hongrois, le Parlement a adopté plusieurs lois renforçant la lutte contre la corruption, afin de permettre à Budapest d’accéder aux 16 milliards d’euros de fonds européens gelés.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le bilan des frappes russes de mardi s’élève à quatorze morts
lemonde.description: Six personnes ont été tuées, mardi, dans l’oblast de Dnipropetrovsk − trois dans la région de Nikpol, et trois dans la ville de Kryvy Rih. Les attaques russes du jour sur l’Ukraine ont aussi causé la mort de huit autres personnes, à Kherson, Odessa ou encore Sloviansk.

lemonde.title: Pesticides : condamné à réviser les autorisations de mise sur le marché, l’Etat propose de réévaluer sept produits, soit 0,28 % des tonnages utilisés
lemonde.description: Les associations à l’origine de l’affaire « Justice pour le vivant » vont de nouveau aller devant le tribunal pour dénoncer les « insuffisances » du plan d’action du gouvernement en matière d’évaluation des risques des pesticides, auquel « Le Monde » a eu accès.

lemonde.title: VIDEO Donald Trump critiqué après les travaux du bassin du Lincoln Memorial
lemonde.description: Ce gigantesque miroir d’eau est envahi par les algues et voit la peinture bleue du revêtement tout récemment posé se décoller. Les travaux voulus par le président américain s’élèvent à plus de 14 millions de dollars.

lemonde.title: Face à l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle, Cate Blanchett lance un site pour faire valoir les droits de chacun
lemonde.description: Présenté comme un « registre du consentement humain » par l’actrice australienne, ce portail en ligne propose à tout individu d’enregistrer les éléments qui forment son identité et d’autoriser ou d’interdire leur utilisation par les systèmes d’IA.

lemonde.title: Au Texas, des personnes accusées de l’attaque d’un centre de rétention de la police de l’immigration condamnées à des peines de trente à cent ans de prison
lemonde.description: Les huit accusés ont été considérés comme appartenant à « une cellule antifa ». Depuis un décret de Donald Trump adopté en septembre 2025, la mouvance antifa est classée comme une « organisation terroriste ».

lemonde.title: « L’étagère du bas, c’est ma salle de bains » : le 10 mètres carrés parisien de Léa, toute jeune avocate
lemonde.description: « Et toi, t’habites où ? ». En pleine crise du logement, étudiants et jeunes actifs redéfinissent, souvent malgré eux, l’art de trouver un chez-soi. Cette semaine, Léa, 28 ans, originaire de Tours, raconte son attachement à son 10 mètres carrés, sans lequel elle n’aurait pas pu faire ses études de droit à la Sorbonne.

lemonde.title: Loi de programmation militaire : les parlementaires s’accordent sur une hausse du budget des armées
lemonde.description: Sept députés et sept sénateurs se sont accordés sur une actualisation de la loi de programmation militaire. Leur mouture devra encore être adoptée le 30 juin au Sénat, puis le lendemain à l’Assemblée, Emmanuel Macron espérant la promulguer symboliquement avant le 14 juillet.

guardian.title: Montreal mayor calls for end to random police checks amid racial profiling investigation
guardian.description:
City’s police force faces investigation of 16 officers accused of disproportionately targeting Black and Arab residents

Montreal’s mayor has called for a halt to random police checks as the city’s police force grapples with an internal investigation into racism and racial profiling by 16 officers.

Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada told reporters last week that her husband, who is Black, had been repeatedly stopped by police while driving.

guardian.title: ‘Cruel hoax’: Canadian healthcare staff decry employer’s email promising fake day off
guardian.description:
Unions condemn ‘insensitive’ internal cybersecurity test sent to healthcare workers in Newfoundland and Labrador

For years, healthcare staff in the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador have felt overworked and underappreciated. Turnover, burnout and thinning resources were pushing workers in the sector to a breaking point.

So when the email titled “June Holiday” arrived in thousands of inboxes, they felt a moment of overdue joy.

guardian.description:
Written in 1947, Kiyoshi Tanimoto’s account of the horrors of the atomic bomb attack will be published in August and is being made into a film

guardian.title: Dutch PM apologises for Moluccan soldiers’ mistreatment after Indonesian independence
guardian.description:
Rob Jetten acknowledges grief and pain of Moluccan families as crowdfunded monument unveiled in Rotterdam

The Dutch prime minister, Rob Jetten, has formally apologised for the “heartless” mistreatment of thousands of Moluccan soldiers who fought for the Dutch colonial army during Indonesia’s struggle for independence.

guardian.title: Weather tracker: Severe thunderstorms sweep Europe and east Asia
guardian.description:
Strong winds and heavy rain batter Slovenia, while France experiences atypical heatwave

Severe thunderstorms swept across the Balkans last week, bringing widespread destruction to parts of the region. The storms developed as unstable hot air lingered over the Adriatic Sea while a cold front plunged south-eastward.

The activewear brand Lululemon has apologised after a promotional event held on the Great Wall of China appeared to mistakenly feature a Japanese drum, prompting an uproar.

guardian.title: Vietnam police rescue hundreds of cats stolen for meat by crime ring
guardian.description:
Major operation launched after spate of pet thefts in Ho Chi Minh City, according to local media

Police in Vietnam have rescued more than 400 cats in a bust of a cat meat crime ring in Ho Chi Minh City, according to animal welfare groups and local media reports.

More than 40 cats were reunited with their owners after the multiday operation last week, but several dozen of those rescued have died due to the harsh conditions in which they were found, the groups said.

Curtin University researchers use innovative techniques to date three-billion-year-old impact crater in Pilbara region

A meteorite that struck Earth three billion years ago left behind a “smoking gun” – evidence of the world’s oldest impact crater in a remote part of Australia.

france24fr.description: Bousculée, la Croatie a obtenu l'essentiel face à une équipe du Panama accrocheuse (1-0), mardi 23 juin à Toronto lors de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes. L'attaquant Ante Budimir, entré à la pause, a débloqué la rencontre pour la Croatie sur un superbe centre de Stanisic (54e). Ce succès permet aux Croates de se relancer avant la dernière journée, alors que le Panama est lui éliminé de la Coupe du monde 2026.

france24fr.title: Colombie - RD Congo en direct : les Cafeteros jouent leur qualification face aux Léopards
france24fr.description: La RD Congo s'apprête croiser la route de la Colombie, mercredi, au stade de Guadalajara à Zapopan. Les Cafeteros peuvent déjà se qualifier pour les 16es de finale en cas de victoire, mais ils devront dominer des Léopards qui ont tenu en échec le Portugal. Suivez la rencontre en live grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: En Corée du Nord, Kim Jong-un annonce équiper la marine d'armes nucléaires
france24fr.description: Des navires militaires nord-coréens sont en train d'être équipés d'armes nucléaires, a affirmé le dirigeant Kim Jong-un mardi. Il a également annoncé le lancement futur de navires de guerre stratégiques de 10 000 tonnes.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'engouement autour des Léopards de RDC explose
france24fr.description: En RDC, après le match nul historique des Léopards face au Portugal la semaine dernière, l'engouement des supporters autour de la sélection nationale est à son comble. Dans l'Est du pays, cette ferveur se heurte à une autre réalité : le prix des maillots des Léopards. La RDC affronte la Colombie à 2h GMT ce mercredi, pour son deuxième match de groupe.

france24fr.title: France : plus de canicules en 16 ans qu'en 60 ans !
france24fr.description: Depuis plusieurs jours, la France suffoque : canicule précoce en mai, puis de nouveau en juin, les records de températures sont battus les uns après les autres. Ce n'est pas nouveau mais le phénomène s'accélère dangereusement. Si bien que ces épisodes de chaleur ne sont plus des accidents du climat mais ils sont devenus la nouvelle norme.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : l'Angleterre frustrée et tenue en échec par le Ghana
Mondial 2026 : l'Angleterre frustrée et tenue en échec par un solide Ghana
france24fr.description: L'Angleterre n'a pas réussi à faire la différence face à une équipe du Ghana disciplinée (0-0), mardi 23 juin à Foxborough lors de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes. Un match nul aux airs d'exploit pour les Black Stars, mais qui n'arrange aucune des deux équipes qui devront encore patienter pour s'adjuger la première place du groupe.

france24fr.title: Enlevée en février, la mère de Savannah Guthrie serait décédée, selon une note de ses ravisseurs
france24fr.description: Une des deux notes envoyées à la famille dans les semaines suivant l'enlèvement de Nancy Guthrie, la mère de la célèbre journaliste américaine Savannah Guthrie, indiquait que l'octogénaire était morte, révèlent mardi plusieurs médias américains. Ses ravisseurs n'ont toujours pas identifié.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : après sa défaite 2-3 face à la Norvège, le Sénégal est au bord de l'élimination
france24fr.description: La nuit a été cauchemardesque pour les supporters sénégalais après la défaite 3 buts à 2 des Lions de la Teranga face à la Norvège. Le Sénégal qui enchaîne une 2e défaite de suite dans cette entame de Coupe du monde et qui se met en danger pour une qualification au 2e tour.

france24fr.title: Marc Bloch au Panthéon : Macron salue son engagement contre "l'esprit de défaite"
france24fr.description: Quatre-vingt-deux ans après son exécution par la Gestapo, l'historien et résistant Marc Bloch a fait son entrée le 23 juin au Panthéon. Professeur spécialiste de l'histoire du Moyen Âge, combattant lors de la Première et de la Seconde Guerre mondiale, il n'a eu de cesse tout au long de sa vie de s'engager pour la France.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Didier Deschamps rentre en France suite au décès de sa mère et sera absent contre la Norvège
Mondial 2026 : Didier Deschamps rentre en France après le décès de sa mère
france24fr.description: Le sélectionneur de l'équipe de France Didier Deschamps a été endeuillé par le décès de sa mère et va rentrer en France pour assister à ses obsèques, a annoncé mardi la Fédération française de football (FFF), qui précise qu'il ne dirigera pas les Bleus contre la Norvège vendredi lors du dernier match du groupe de la France au Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: Comment la désinformation sexiste a envahi la Coupe du monde
france24fr.description: Depuis le début de la Coupe du Monde, des vidéos de supportrices inondent les réseaux sociaux. Problème: elles sont toutes générées par l'Intelligence artificielle. Véhiculant une image hypersexualisée des femmes, elles permettent à leurs créateurs de gagner de l'argent grâce aux vues qu'elles génèrent. Décryptage dans Info Intox avec Jules BOITEAU.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Portugal se balade contre l'Ouzbékistan, doublé pour Cristiano Ronaldo
france24fr.description: La Seleçao n'a laissé aucune chance à l'Ouzbékistan (5-0), mardi 23 juin au stade de Houston, lors de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes. Le capitaine portugais Cristiano Ronaldo (41 ans) a ouvert le score dès la 6e minute, puis inscrit un doublé juste avant la pause (39e). Ces deux nouvelles réalisations font de lui le premier joueur de l'histoire à marquer lors de six Coupes du monde.

france24fr.title: Angleterre - Ghana : revivez le match nul entre les Three Lions et les Black Stars
france24fr.description: L'Angleterre et le Ghana se sont quittés sur un match nul au terme d'un choc qui a longtemps connu un faux rythme avant de s'emballer dans le dernier quart d'heure au stade de Foxborough, lors de la deuxième journée de la phase de groupes du Mondial 2026. Revivez le match commenté par nos confrères de RFI.

france24fr.title: Canicule : va-t-on enfin se réveiller ?
france24fr.description: Après des records de température enregistrés lundi et de nouveaux décès liés à la chaleur, la canicule exceptionnelle qui frappe la France s'étend encore un peu plus ce mardi. Les infrastructures et les organismes sont mis à rude épreuve. Sébastien Lecornu a annoncé un renforcement de la mobilisation du système de santé en activant le plan Orsan au niveau 2 sur 4.

france24fr.title: Canicule: la flore et la faune souffrent aussi de la chaleur
france24fr.description: La chaleur exceptionnelle de ce début d'été assèche les sols et entraîne une mortalité accrue de la végétation. Avec la multiplication de ces événements extrêmes, les écosystèmes migrent vers le nord. Les platanes et chênes ne peuvent pas survivre à ces coups de chaud répétés. Les animaux qui dépendent de ces arbres vont donc se déplacer là où ils peuvent survivre. La modification du climat est en train de transformer les paysages que nous connaissons.

zeit.title: Aufrüstung: Pistorius plant laut Berichten Aus für Fregattenprojekt F126
zeit.description: Es sollte das größte Rüstungsprojekt in der Geschichte der Marine werden: neue Fregatten vom Typ F126. Nun will Verteidigungsminister Boris Pistorius offenbar aussteigen.

zeit.description: Nach dem bundesweiten Ausfall sind wieder Züge der Deutschen Bahn unterwegs. Ein Sprecher teilte mit, dass die Ursache gefunden und die Störung behoben worden sei.

zeit.title: Hitze in Europa: Großbritannien schließt Schulen wegen Hitzewelle
zeit.description: Der britische Wetterdienst rechnet mit neuen Temperaturrekorden und hat die höchste Hitzewarnstufe verhängt. Im Westen Deutschlands könnte es schwere Hitzegewitter geben.

zeit.title: Deutsche Bahn: Bahnverkehr steht wegen technischer Störung bundesweit still
zeit.description: Eine Funkstörung hat den Zugverkehr bundesweit zum Erliegen gebracht, S-Bahnen und Fernzüge können nicht weiterfahren. Laut der Bahn wurde die Ursache nun gefunden.

nzz.title: Houston, wir hatten ein Problem: Cristiano Ronaldo beendet mit historischen Toren vorerst alle Rentendebatten
nzz.description: «I'm back», triumphiert der 41-Jährige nach seiner Gala gegen Usbekistan und widerlegt Berichte über Unstimmigkeiten in Portugals Team. Nur das M-Wort mag er partout nicht hören.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Über tausend Schiffe sollen noch im Persischen Golf festsitzen +++11 000 Seeleute sollen evakuieren werden
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Die Folgen sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.title: Deutschland: Bahnverkehr läuft nach bundesweiter Funkstörung wieder an
nzz.description: Am Dienstagabend stand der Bahnverkehr in ganz Deutschland still. Inzwischen läuft er schrittweise wieder an.

nzz.title: Die Zürcher FDP nominiert Andri Silberschmidt und Martin Huber für den Regierungsrat
nzz.description: An einer heissen Delegiertenversammlung haben die Freisinnigen den Neftenbacher Landwirt Martin Huber als zweiten Regierungsratskandidaten gekürt. Der Favorit Andri Silberschmidt wurde im ersten Wahlgang gewählt.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - Sprit- und Gaspreise deutlich gesunken – die aktuellen Zahlen zur Energieversorgung in Deutschland
nzz.description: Wie wirken sich Energiewende und globale Krisen auf Strom- und Gaspreise aus? Hier gibt es jeden Tag die aktuellen Zahlen.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: Wo sich die Hitze aushalten lässt: die schönsten Badis von Zürich
nzz.description: In Zürich ist das Wasser nie weit: Die Stadt ist so reich an Freibädern wie kaum eine andere in Europa. Wir zeigen die schönsten Anlagen.

nzz.title: Vermisstes Kind tot aus der Reuss geborgen
nzz.description: Dutzende von freiwilligen Helfern hatten tagelang nach einem Buben gesucht. Bei dem am Dienstag gefundenen Kind dürfte es sich um den vermissten 5-Jährigen handeln.

nzz.title: Wer ist der Beste, Messi oder Mbappé? Zwei Superstars kämpfen um die WM-Torjägerkrone
nzz.description: Die Weltmeisterschaft wird zum Generationenduell. Lionel Messi bricht den WM-Torrekord, doch Kylian Mbappé jagt ihn – die Zeit spielt für den Franzosen.

nzz.title: Versteckspiel um Taliban-Besuch bei der EU: Ohne Gegenleistungen wollen die Islamisten nicht über Ausschaffungen reden
nzz.description: Unter grosser Geheimhaltung sind Vertreter der afghanischen De-facto-Regierung nach Brüssel gereist. Die EU-Staaten sind auf ihre Mitarbeit angewiesen, wollen sie aber nicht diplomatisch anerkennen.

nzz.title: Zweifel an Unabhängigkeit und Unparteilichkeit: Das Bundesgericht setzt die Genfer Staatsanwaltschaft in einem Betrugsfall in den Ausstand
nzz.description: Die höchsten Richter haben der Verteidigung recht gegeben. Denn es geht um den Vater des Generalstaatsanwalts Olivier Jornot.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Frische Idee für die Steuern: Überschüsse gehören den Bürgern
nzz.description: Der Kampf gegen die Steuer- und Abgabenlast ist ein urliberales Anliegen. Es ist erfreulich, dass die FDP das erkannt hat.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Nicht reden, sondern umsetzen: Die Rentenreform liefert die Chance, die Stimmung im Land zu drehen
nzz.description: Die Gremium hat geliefert, woran Vorgängerregierungen jahrzehntelang gescheitert sind. Kanzler Friedrich Merz könnte sich nun als echter Reformer profilieren – wenn er die nötige Durchsetzungskraft besitzt.

nzz.title: 15-Jähriger ertrinkt in der Limmat, ein Kollege filmt den Sprung und alarmiert die Polizei erst nach 27 Minuten
nzz.description: Ein 20-jähriger Angolaner steht wegen Unterlassung der Nothilfe vor dem Bezirksgericht Zürich. Die Staatsanwältin verlangt sechs Monate Freiheitsstrafe.

spiegel.title: Mexiko: Unberührte Maya-Stätte im Dschungel entdeckt
spiegel.description: Palastartige Gebäude, Wasserkanäle, ein Stein mit eingravierter Enthauptungsszene: Forscher haben in Mexikos Wildnis einen Komplex der Maya gefunden. Die isolierte Lage hatte offenbar Plünderer ferngehalten.

spiegel.title: Stadt Halle (Saale) fordert Strand-Bad auf, umstrittene Einlass-Regel zu Deutsch-Kenntnissen zurückzunehmen
spiegel.description: Nur wer gut genug Deutsch kann, wird in ein Strandbad in Halle an der Saale gelassen. Das sorgte für scharfe Kritik. Jetzt schaltet sich die Stadt ein. Sie ist offenbar um ihr Ansehen besorgt.

spiegel.title: Insgesamt 450 Jahre Haft für acht »Antifa-Terroristen« in Texas
spiegel.description: Ein Mann soll auf einen Vollzugsbeamten geschossen haben, andere Demonstranten zündeten Feuerwerkskörper. Ein Gericht in Texas hat acht Aktivisten dafür zu langen Gefängnisstrafen verurteilt. Kritiker sprechen von politischer Justiz.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: Kroatien gegen Panama, Kolumbien gegen DR Kongo
spiegel.description: Nach der Auftaktniederlage gegen England hat Kroatien sein zweites Vorrundenspiel gegen Panama gewonnen. Kolumbien stünde mit einem Sieg gegen DR Kongo in der K.o.-Phase. Alles Wichtige im Livekommentar.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: England und Thomas Tuchel enttäuschen gegen Ghana
spiegel.description: Thomas Tuchels Engländer begeisterten zum WM-Auftakt gegen Kroatien – davon war gegen Ghana kaum etwas zu sehen. Immerhin konnte sich der Trainer der Three Lions abseits des Rasens durchsetzen: gegen die Fotografen.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Erst Züge fahren wieder nach bundesweitem Ausfall wieder
spiegel.description: Im ganzen Land standen Züge der Deutschen Bahn für rund anderthalb Stunden still. Nun rollen die ersten zwar wieder. Es wird aber noch lange mit Verspätungen und Ausfällen gerechnet. Die Ursache der Störung ist offenbar gefunden.

spiegel.title: Alibaba: Konzern verklagt US-Regierung gegen Einstufung als chinesisches Militärunternehmen
spiegel.description: Alibaba wehrt sich gegen seine Aufnahme auf eine Pentagon-Liste mutmaßlicher chinesischer Militärunternehmen. Der Konzern spricht von einer unbegründeten Einstufung und warnt vor schweren Schäden für sein US-Geschäft.

spiegel.title: Deutsche Bahn: Bundesweiter Ausfall des Zugfunks legt Bahnverkehr lahm
spiegel.description: Bundesweite IT-Probleme bei der Bahn sorgen für erhebliche Einschränkungen im Zugverkehr. Nach Angaben des Konzerns sind interne Kommunikationssysteme betroffen, Züge werden aus Sicherheitsgründen zurückgehalten. Die Ursache ist unklar.

spiegel.title: Georgia Meloni setzt im Streit mit Donald Trump nun auf Deeskalation
spiegel.description: Trump behauptet, Meloni habe ihn beim G7-Gipfel um ein Foto angefleht. Ihre Reaktion? Deutlich und scharf – doch Italiens Regierungschefin will den Zwist jetzt offenbar nicht weiter ausufern lassen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Cristiano Ronaldo führt Portugal mit zwei Toren zu Sieg gegen Usbekistan
spiegel.description: Der verpatzte WM-Auftakt der Portugiesen wurde eng mit der schwachen Leistung Cristiano Ronaldos verknüpft. Gegen Usbekistan zeigte CR7 nun, dass er sein Ego zurückstellen kann – und schrieb Geschichte.

spiegel.title: Österreich: Bremer Schulklasse gerät bei Gewitter in Bergnot
spiegel.description: Gewitter sind in den Alpen eine echte Gefahr. Eine Schulklasse aus Deutschland geriet nun im Nachbarland durch Blitz und Donner in Bedrängnis. Ein Notruf folgte.

spiegel.title: Niedersachsen: Stichflamme beim Grillen – Elfjähriger rettet sich in Kanal
spiegel.description: Bei einem Grilltreffen in Niedersachsen ist ein Junge durch eine Stichflamme schwer verletzt worden. Um sich vor den Flammen zu retten, ist er ins Wasser gesprungen. Ein 17-Jähriger soll die Feuerflamme verursacht haben.

spiegel.title: Boris Pistorius: Der Verteidigungsminister will das Fregatten-Projekt F126 beenden
spiegel.description: SPD-Verteidigungsminister Pistorius plant, aus dem größten Rüstungsprojekt in der Geschichte der Marine auszusteigen. Der Schaden würde in die Milliarden gehen. Und auch die möglichen Ersatzkriegsschiffe werden teurer.

spiegel.title: Kenia: Proteste erzwingen Entschuldigung im Streit um Ebola-Zentrum
spiegel.description: Wochenlang haben Menschen in Kenia wegen eines Ebola-Isolierzentrums protestiert, das nur US-Amerikanern zugutekommen sollte. Ein Minister wollte das Projekt unbedingt durchdrücken – und musste sich jetzt entschuldigen.

spiegel.title: Gespräche mit Taliban: Vertreter erstmals in Brüssel empfangen
spiegel.description: Erstmals seit ihrer Rückkehr an die Macht sind Taliban zu Gesprächen in Brüssel empfangen worden. Die EU spricht von einem technischen Austausch über Abschiebungen nach Afghanistan – das Treffen steht jedoch in der Kritik.

spiegel.title: Straße von Hormus: Weltschifffahrtsorganisation will 11.000 festsitzende Seeleute evakuieren
spiegel.description: Für Tausende Seeleute an Bord von Tankern und Frachtern war die Blockade der Straße von Hormus eine besondere Belastung, sie saßen fest. Nun sollen sie nach Hause kommen.

spiegel.title: Korsika: Eine autonome Insel? Frankreichs Unterhaus billigt Pläne
spiegel.description: Das Verhältnis zwischen Paris und Ajaccio gilt als schwierig. Die Mittelmeerinsel will mehr Freiheiten. Frankreichs Nationalversammlung stimmt dem Wunsch zu, doch es gibt noch Hürden zu überwinden.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz und die Rente: Endlich mal ein guter Tag für den CDU-Kanzler
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler könnte Aufbruchstimmung verbreiten, Optimismus versprühen, aber es gelingt ihm nicht. Ein fast trauriger Ernst scheint ihn befallen zu haben, und er kann ihn nicht abschütteln.

observador.description: Na Europa, à arrogância de recusar como possível tudo o que foge das nossas categorias intelectuais, segue-se a fraqueza de ser incapaz de combater uma das maiores ameaças.

observador.description: O trineto da Princesa Isabel e do Conde d'Eu foi impedido de entrar no Palácio do Grão-Pará, no centro de Petrópolis, onde alega viver há mais de 40 anos. O pai e os tios trocaram a fechadura da casa.

observador.description: A letargia do PSD coloca como possibilidade cada vez mais real a sua substituição pelo Chega.

observador.description: Benjamin Song, que disparou contra um polícia, recebeu 100 anos de prisão. Administração Trump elogiou sentenças. Penas ultrapassam condenações relacionadas com o ataque ao Capitólio em 2021.

observador.description: O Estado cobra impostos sobre lucros e salários, cobra taxas, licenças, contribuições e burocracias. Depois anuncia que vai devolver uma pequena parcela desse dinheiro em apoios.

observador.description: O presente já é eletrodigital, e o futuro será ainda mais.

observador.description: Há qualquer coisa de profundamente portuguesa nesta história. Não porque os políticos mudem de opinião, mas porque o façam com a tranquilidade de quem muda de fila no supermercado.

observador.description: Onde a escala é uma questão de sobrevivência e de competitividade, a Europa escolheu a dispersão e o espartilho regulatório.

letemps.description:

new-sci.description: A spider living in the rainforests of Queensland, Australia, builds a snare trap reminiscent of a Roman-era ballista weapon that it uses to catapult green tree ants into a web 30 centimetres above

new-sci.title: How menopause radically changes the brain – and what happens after
new-sci.description: The brain undergoes a full renovation during menopause. Although these changes are profound, we’re learning that the long-term impact needn’t be all bad

new-sci.title: ‘Fusogenic’ neurosurgery let paralysed pigs walk again – are we next?
new-sci.description: Researchers say a surgery that let pigs with completely severed spinal cords walk again may lead to human trials, and then perhaps even full head or brain transplants. Columnist Helen Thomson is intrigued but sceptical of whether the technique can be successful in humans

new-sci.title: A promising natural technique to remove CO2 could backfire
new-sci.description: Several start-ups have tried to grow seaweed to remove atmospheric CO2, but this could affect the levels of nutrients in the ocean and hamper other CO2-sucking processes

new-sci.title: The surprising ways your brain changes from your 20s to your 40s
new-sci.description: When does your brain reach adulthood? We're now understanding the many ways the organ continues to mature decades after society first deems you an adult

new-sci.title: People training new AI models admit they just get chatbots to do it
new-sci.description: The next generation of AI models are meant to be trained by people paid to have conversations with them, but several of these workers have admitted to New Scientist that they simply get chatbots to do it instead. new-sci.title: We've found a mysterious substance on Titan and Pluto
new-sci.description: Something is absorbing light on the surfaces of Pluto and Saturn’s moon Titan, and figuring out what it is could be crucial to understanding Titan’s complex chemistry

new-sci.title: Autism may have two distinct subtypes that vary by brain activity
new-sci.description: Evidence is mounting that there are distinct subtypes of autism, and now, scientists have found that the condition can vary according to the strength of people's brain connections

new-sci.title: A quantum state that lasts forever may finally be within our grasp
new-sci.description: Defying the laws of thermodynamics, experiments are beginning to show that a quantum state that is frozen forever might not be impossible. If we can tame it, it could unlock whole new types of matter

new-sci.title: The one film to watch before seeing Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day
new-sci.description: With Steven Spielberg’s new extraterrestrial film Disclosure Day just out, it’s the ideal time to watch Close Encounters of the Third Kind – perhaps the perfect UFO film, says film columnist Bethan Ackerley

phys-org.title: A new 'prescription' to address the environmental crisis
phys-org.description: A new "prescription for the planet" aims to address the deepening environmental crisis.

phys-org.title: How sperm whale vocal dialects evolve as they adopt new calls while still remembering the old
phys-org.description: New research from the University of St. Andrews shows how sperm whale vocal dialects evolve as they adopt new calls while still remembering the old. An international team of researchers studying vocal dialects in the endangered population of sperm whales that live in the Mediterranean Sea has captured the cultural evolution of new dialects in process.

phys-org.title: Simple acknowledgment boosts repeat customer participation in take-back programs
phys-org.description: Companies may only need to send an acknowledgment message to boost repeat customer participation in recycling and reuse programs for used goods like laptops and coffee pods, according to a new study led by Penn State researchers. The idea for the study arose over a cup of coffee—more specifically, the single-use pod used to make the coffee. phys-org.title: Listening for quantum oscillations in the Kondo insulator ytterbium dodecaboride
phys-org.description: Magnetic quantum oscillations have been unexpectedly observed in insulators, where freely moving charge carriers are not expected to exist. A joint study by researchers from Tokyo University of Science, The University of Tokyo and Kobe University investigated this puzzling behavior in the Kondo insulator YbB12 using ultrasound.

phys-org.title: This tiny Australian spider uses a high‑powered web catapult to trap and eat aggressive ants
phys-org.description: There's more than one way a spider can spin its web. Some construct large vertical orb webs, while others build horizontal sheet webs or tangled cobwebs that ensnare crawling insects.

phys-org.title: How reading shapes and enhances our cognitive activity
phys-org.description: Smartphones, online learning, generative AI: The way we read has changed more in the last decade than in the previous century. So what do we actually know about what reading does for the mind? In his new book, Falk Huettig, senior investigator at the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics, brings together research spanning psychology, linguistics, neuroscience and education to answer that question. The result is a systematic account of how literacy reshapes memory, attention, language proces

phys-org.title: Four-decade mystery solved as PKCβ structure reveals new drug target
phys-org.description: After nearly four decades of research, Mayo Clinic scientists have revealed the molecular structure of protein kinase C beta (PKCβ), a key protein linked to cancer and neurological diseases. The findings, published in Nature Communications, provide the first detailed view of how the protein works and how the breast cancer drug endoxifen can target it.

phys-org.title: Physical pressure helps pathogenic P. aeruginosa survive antibiotic treatment
phys-org.description: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is an opportunistic pathogen that can cause acute and chronic infections. Responsible for many hospital-acquired infections, it is also a major concern for people with cystic fibrosis, whose lungs are clogged with thick mucus that promotes its growth.

phys-org.title: Researchers aim for hardier herds of worms for productive, resilient farming practice
phys-org.description: The black soldier fly converts organic waste into biomass. The cricket brings crunchy protein to the dinner plate. The mealworm can break down plastic.

phys-org.title: People care more about being right than avoiding mistakes, study finds
phys-org.description: Conventional wisdom says the best predictions are the ones that minimize mistakes, but new research suggests that is not necessarily how people see it. A study published in Management Science has found that when people make or evaluate predictions, they care more about the possibility of being exactly right than about reducing the size of potential errors. phys-org.title: Is political polarization dangerous? Study provides clearer answers
phys-org.description: In recent years, political polarization has received considerable attention, not least as an explanation for developments in the United States.

phys-org.title: Chloroplast study reveals molecular lock that helps power life on Earth
phys-org.description: A new study reveals the dynamics of photosynthesis at the cellular level. Led by co-authors Professor Barry Bruce and Associate Professor Rajan Lamichhane, both of the Department of Biochemistry and Cellular and Molecular Biology (BCMB) at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, the team published its findings—"Single-molecule fluorescence and cross-linking reveal ligand-gated Toc34 oligomerization dynamics"—in the Biophysical Journal. phys-org.title: Why warmer seas may not wipe out female fish in some species
phys-org.description: In many fish species, water temperature determines the sex of the fry. This biological mechanism threatens to wipe out entire populations because of a shortage of females in the face of global warming. However, an international study conducted in Spain, France and Brazil has found that this well-known masculinization effect can be offset over generations. phys-org.title: Brain growth may explain why birds lay outsized eggs compared with dinosaurs
phys-org.description: A new study has uncovered a fundamental link between brain size and offspring size, helping to solve a long-standing evolutionary puzzle: Why do birds lay such disproportionately large eggs?

phys-org.title: Animals are often moved to make way for infrastructure, but we don't know what happens to them next
phys-org.description: When major infrastructure projects are built in rural areas, wildlife is often displaced and moved out of the way. This is called mitigation translocation, and it is a globally recognized method for moving animals. However, not everyone applies it the same way, or at all.

phys-org.title: Self-driving chemistry lab discovers catalysts that can switch products on demand
phys-org.description: Researchers have developed a self-driving chemistry lab that can autonomously search through hundreds of catalyst recipes and reaction conditions to identify faster, more selective and more programmable ways to make important industrial chemicals. The work could accelerate catalyst discovery for industries ranging from pharmaceuticals and plastics to fuels and specialty chemicals.

phys-org.title: Heat wave sparks health warnings across Europe
phys-org.description: Workers sweated in choking heat and pupils stayed home Tuesday as an early-summer heat wave smothered much of Europe, with France suffering its hottest day on record.

phys-org.title: Drug peptides defy shape rules, activating receptors without full spiral form
phys-org.description: When many of us think about how drugs work in the body, we may first think about how a drug gets into the body, such as a pill versus an injection. In the Gellman Group at the UW–Madison Department of Chemistry, researchers are instead thinking about how a drug behaves after it reaches its target, which is critical for effective drug performance. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20569v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze identifiability in co-adaptive human-machine systems. We show that closed-loop encoder estimates do not uniquely identify user adaptation, but instead reflect properties of the joint system. We discuss implications for interpreting behavioral adaptation and propose conditions for identification.

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20600v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What can the success of modern AI tell us about how humans learn? This paper argues that taking AI seriously as a model of human learning supports a modest but genuine associationism. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20615v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents now participate as first-class team members across the software development lifecycle, yet no specification language exists for expressing the human-agent responsibility boundaries, approval gates, and governance constraints this collaboration requires. arxiv-ai.title: PEAR: Permutation-Equivariant Adaptive Routing Multi-Agent Debate
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20621v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent debate improves the reliability of large language models (LLMs) through iterative peer critiques. arxiv-ai.title: Darwin Mobile Agent: A Roadmap for Self-Evolution
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20622v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The goal of artificial intelligence is to create agents capable of general, adaptive behaviour in open-ended environments. Guided by the "Bitter Lesson", we argue that the most effective path toward this goal is to systematically remove human priors and allow intelligence to naturally emerge through interaction with a "Big World" that is orders of magnitude more complex than the agent itself. arxiv-ai.title: Path-dependent program induction under resource constraints explains human sequence learning
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20623v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How do people build abstract, reusable knowledge from sequential experience under bounded cognitive resources? arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20624v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Significant progress has been made in aligning LLMs with target value functions. We argue that, even when an LLM has been well aligned in (post-)training, it may still fail to maximise the aligned value in reasoning. arxiv-ai.title: AlphaMemo: Structured Search-Process Memory for Self-Evolving Alpha Mining Agents
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20625v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are promising for alpha mining via combining financial priors, symbolic reasoning, executable factor generation, and feedback-driven refinement. Yet, they face a combinatorial search space, noisy non-stationary feedback, redundant discoveries, and overfitting risks from naively reusing past successes. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20627v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Planning with world models is bottlenecked by compounding prediction errors and the difficulty of defining optimizable goals. Visual targets provide precise local gradients but poor distant guidance, while language is flexible yet limited by noisy cross-modal alignment or dependence on large generative models unsuited for the high-sampling nature of model-based planning. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20628v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Humans increasingly make decisions with AI assistance; for example, doctors may follow AI-recommended diagnostic tests and base their diagnoses on the results. arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent-runtime systems emit traces, ledgers, provenance graphs, policy logs, delegation tokens, cache events, and tool-firewall records, but those containers do not necessarily answer governance questions about a specific decision. arxiv-ai.title: SkillHarness: Harnessing Safe Skills for Computer-Use Agents
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20636v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) are increasingly deployed in dynamic interactive environments, creating a growing need for continual skill learning during interaction. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20637v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electoral redistricting in Ireland's Proportional Representation Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) system faces the challenge of selecting an optimally representative set of electoral boundaries from an enormous set of possible configurations, and where ``representative'' is a delicate balance of constitutional objectives that are often in tension with one another. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20638v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as long-lived agents that must adapt across users, tasks, domains, modalities, and feedback regimes without access to model weights. arxiv-ai.title: An LLM-Explainable DRL Framework for Passenger-Directed Autonomous Driving
arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20640v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous vehicles offer the potential for safer and more efficient mobility, yet public trust remains limited due to the lack of transparency in their decision-making. arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.20642v1 Announce Type: new

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.

proj-syn.title: Alan Greenspan’s Mixed Legacy
proj-syn.description: The longtime Federal Reserve chair inferred from past crises that lightly regulated markets, while prone to excesses, could right themselves sufficiently to avoid imperiling the financial system and the economy. The correct lesson would have been that markets require strict regulation, and that competent technocrats are essential.

proj-syn.title: Will AI Yield Abundance Without Purpose?
proj-syn.description: Work and employment play a uniquely powerful role in structuring people’s days and conferring a sense of belonging, status, and self-worth. Although AI boosters insist that people would organically find new sources of meaning if most jobs are automated, there is no reason to assume so.

proj-syn.title: To Avoid Climate Peril, the World Must Electrify
proj-syn.description: The war in the Gulf has unleashed powerful market forces that the rest of the world can harness to accelerate electrification and keep the Paris climate agreement's primary objectives on track. Doing so will not only mitigate climate change, but also strengthen economic resilience worldwide.

proj-syn.title: What the Iran War Taught the World About Food Security
proj-syn.description: Perhaps the most unsettling lesson from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the gap between what we knew and how we prepared. Countries should use whatever easing of immediate pressures occurs to strengthen resilience before the next shock arrives.

proj-syn.title: The Orange Bandit
proj-syn.description: According to the Roman Emperor Tiberius, a ruler can either “shear the sheep” for many years, by encouraging productive activity from which to generate tax revenues, or he can “skin them alive” just once. By brazenly using the US government to pillage the country, President Donald Trump has apparently chosen the knife.

proj-syn.title: How (Not) to Conserve Tropical Forests
proj-syn.description: Although the Tropical Forest Forever Facility that emerged from the last United Nations Climate Conference is unlikely to succeed, critically important global conservation efforts are not doomed. Through sustainability-linked sovereign bonds and loans, tropical countries can overcome the TFFF’s fatal flaws.

proj-syn.title: Was Brexit Inevitable?
proj-syn.description: If counterfactual history is motivated by a refusal to accept what many have deemed inevitable, it is newly relevant now that the West is marking the tenth anniversary of the Brexit referendum. Even if Britain's fateful choice was caused by deeper structural and historical forces, that does not justify fatalism.

proj-syn.title: Questioning the Just War Doctrine
proj-syn.description: With war becoming more frequent and more lethal to civilians, Pope Leo XIV and the College of Cardinals are wading into the debate over its legitimacy. The best outcome of the “consistory” Leo is convening in in late June would be to authorize an overhaul of the just war doctrine for the modern era—and ask the necessary questions.

proj-syn.title: Bosnia Must Stand on Its Own
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration's recent, apparently corrupt intervention in Bosnia and Herzegovina could have been an opportunity finally to put the country on a path to full independence after more than 30 years of being a ward of the international community. Instead, the vicious cycle of dependence looks set to continue.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Logic of the AI Arms Race
proj-syn.description: AI and drones are rapidly transforming warfare, shifting military power toward countries that can combine manufacturing scale, advanced AI systems, and battlefield data. The United States and Europe, hobbled by political dysfunction and obsolete military structures, remain dangerously unprepared.

proj-syn.title: The Meaning of Limited Government—Then and Now
proj-syn.description: In 1776, Adam Smith and America’s founders envisioned an economy that allowed individuals to pursue their own material well-being, with minimal government intervention. Today, America’s Republican Party claims to be committed to restoring that laissez-faire ideal, even as they make a mockery of its animating principles.

proj-syn.title: AI Sovereignty Is About Options, Not Ownership
proj-syn.description: The US government’s abrupt decision to suspend foreign access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models clarifies what “AI sovereignty” is really about. In the emerging AI economy, competitive advantage will come not from owning a single model, but from being able to evaluate, select, and orchestrate many models.

proj-syn.title: The Promise and Peril of AGI
proj-syn.description: Artificial general intelligence could dramatically increase human prosperity and free people from countless mundane tasks. But unless its benefits and ownership are broadly shared, it could deprive billions of workers of their livelihoods and pave the way for a new form of techno-authoritarianism.
